key_insight: Wildfire-SSR combines satellite imagery and street-view evidence to assess wildfire vulnerability at individual structures. Its geolocation-aware approach connects neighborhood-scale context with property-level details.
problem_solved: Existing approaches often struggle to capture parcel-scale ignition pathways while maintaining broad geographic coverage across wildland–urban interface communities.
method: Use satellite imagery to capture macro-scale geographic context.
Use street-view imagery to capture micro-scale evidence, with a vision-language model extracting wildfire-relevant information.
Integrate both perspectives through a geolocation-aware multimodal framework for structure-level risk assessment.
impact: The framework illustrates how complementary imagery sources can support fine-grained environmental risk assessment. The supplied abstract is truncated, so performance gains and validation results cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Satellite-to-street-view diagram linking a neighborhood map to an individual building.
Two-stream fusion schematic: satellite context + street-view evidence → structure-level risk.
Conceptual map highlighting individual structures within a wildland–urban interface community.
Scale comparison showing community-level coverage versus parcel-level detail.
paper_title: Wildfire-SSR: Geolocation-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Structure-Level Wildfire Risk Assessment
paper_authors: Yu-Hsuan Ho, Yiming Xiao, Hao-En Lai, Ali Mostafavi, Samuel D. Brody
